tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to...'), focuses on user intent and triggers (why the bill is high, which model costs most, idle PT, quota headroom, etc.) rather than implementation details, and explicitly lists many contexts where it applies including cases where the user wouldn't call it a 'cost review'. It also sets a boundary ('Not for outages happening now'). While dense, it stays as one continuous sentence/paragraph which is acceptable given the breadth of triggers it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low, which model costs the most..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious rules (cost explorer grouping quirks, token-vs-billed divergence, quota code lookup) rather than explaining general concepts. There is no filler explaining what AWS, cost, or tokens are.
tests.evidence: Usage types vary (`-mantle-`, `-standard`, `-flex`, `-priority`, `-cross-region-global`): match a model's lines loosely.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference tables (full API quirks, metric derivations, quota code lists) are consistently pushed to references/ files and only summarized or pointed to in the body; the body's tables (router, check families) are compact summaries, not exhaustive reference data.
tests.evidence: How to read each API and metric: [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) (load it with any row).

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body at least once (e.g., in the Router table, References section, or inline).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the body is paired with a specific trigger condition explaining when to load it, e.g. in the References section and inline mentions.
tests.evidence: Load when the step says so: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding); ... [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) (before interpreting a response; quota lookup §18, Step 6)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only rules, cost labeling, quota lookup, PT resize prohibition) are given exact prescriptive instructions, while flexible analytical judgment areas (e.g., deciding LLM-COST-003/004 applicability) are described with reasoning/criteria rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: PT can't be resized in place (`UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput` changes only the name or model): give the LLM-PT-001 remediation, never an update command.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple rate sources or methods exist, the skill designates a clear priority order/default rather than listing equal options.
tests.evidence: Rates, in order: the user (say so); `pricing:GetProducts` (us-east-1, one call per model...); or the [pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) read with `verify_aws_claim`.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (Steps 1-8, router table mapping question types to reads) applicable to any Bedrock cost/capacity question, not a one-off task for a specific account or resource.
tests.evidence: Run the steps in order. Each step is bounded: a denied API, no datapoints or an unsupported region is recorded as `unavailable` / `not checked` and the review goes on.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has dedicated 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' sections that document concrete, environment-specific pitfalls like ACTIVE status misconceptions and quota naming errors.
tests.evidence: "The PT's model is `ACTIVE`, so it's safe." Models stay `ACTIVE` until end of life: check the EOL announcement (api-quirks §4, LLM-PT-003).

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured cost/capacity reports and explicitly provides a template asset referenced for full reports.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report template is entirely delegated to the assets/ file.
tests.evidence: the whole template lives in assets/capacity-cost-report-template.md, not inline in the body

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is linked in the body with a markdown link.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link clearly specifies it should be loaded only when producing a full report, not generically.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The main procedure is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: - [ ] Step 1: **Scope:** region(s), window, models and profiles; ... - [ ] Step 8: Assemble the findings, then run "Before You Present".

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its own output for errors before presenting.
tests.evidence:
A confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so.
- [ ] Every top rule and "Guardrails — details" holds; no 12-digit number.
